comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The diagnosis holds, and the pin logic writes a correct `root=` line when it is allowed to write. Migrations run as the logged-in user, though, and a few steps in this one assume root. On the machines it targets, the migration either stops the update queue or exits early and is marked done without repairing anything. The repository's `privileged-heredoc-test.sh` also fails on this head.

**Verified:**
- In limine-entry-tool 1.37.1 and 1.39.0 (`ConfigReader.readBootOptions()`), `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and `/proc/cmdline` are consulted only when the effective `KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]` is blank. The `+=` in `omarchy-defaults.conf` alone is enough to make it non-blank.
- `--get-cmdline <kernel>` with one positional argument is the real signature (`Main.java`). The `<profile name>` in the help text is stale.
- Healthy installs are untouched: when `root=` is already effective, the guard exits before any write or rebuild.
- In a synthetic harness (stubbed tools, redirected paths, write access granted), the pin was correct for PARTUUID, btrfs subvolume, resume and derived-UUID layouts. A second run was a no-op, and an encrypted root without unlock parameters was skipped.
- The runner tracks each migration file separately, so this timestamp still runs on machines that already applied newer migrations.

### Writes to `/etc/default/limine` run without privilege

Lines 71-73 run `mkdir -p`, `touch` and `cat >>"$default_conf"` with no elevation. `omarchy-migrate` runs migrations as the calling user under `bash -euo pipefail`, and `omarchy-update`, the upgrade script and the login notifier all invoke it that way. The two Limine tool calls still work because their wrappers re-exec through `sudo`. `touch` and the shell's `>>` redirection have no such path. Other Limine migrations (for example `1789325478.sh`) and `preserve_kernel_cmdline_root` use `sudo` for the same writes.

```text
machine whose effective default cmdline lacks root=, `omarchy update` as a normal user
  L15  limine-entry-tool --get-cmdline default   -> re-execs via sudo, no root= found
  L72  touch /etc/default/limine                 -> Permission denied, script exits 1
       omarchy-migrate aborts; this and every later migration stay pending
```

**Impact:** On a machine this migration targets, nothing is written or rebuilt. `omarchy update` stops with its generic error on every run until the file is fixed by hand.

**Suggested change:** `sudo mkdir -p`, then write with `sudo tee -a "$default_conf" >/dev/null <<EOF_CONF`.

### The `/boot/limine.conf` check cannot see a root-only ESP

Line 13, `[[ -f /boot/limine.conf ]] || exit 0`, runs as the user. The omarchy-iso quattro pre-mounted install writes the ESP with `umask=0077`, and archinstall has mounted EFI partitions with `fmask=0177,dmask=0077` since May 2026. Under those options a normal user cannot traverse `/boot`, so the test is false even when the file exists.

**Impact:** On such machines the migration exits 0 at line 13 and is recorded as complete, so the repair is never evaluated. This path mostly affects hand-ported machines built with a recent archinstall. ISO installs already pin `root=`.

**Suggested change:** `sudo test -f /boot/limine.conf`, matching `as_root test -f` in `preserve_kernel_cmdline_root`.

### A successful `limine-mkinitcpio` exit does not show the UKI was rebuilt

Line 81 turns a failure into a warning, but the larger gap is upstream. In limine-entry-tool 1.37.1 and 1.39.0, `limine-mkinitcpio-install` maps every per-kernel build failure to success: `process_kernel` ends each step with `|| return 0`, and `main` adds `|| true`. After a failed build, the old UKI stays installed.

```text
kernel build fails -> process_kernel returns 0 -> main returns 0 -> limine-mkinitcpio exits 0
  -> migration exits 0, marked complete; old UKI without root= stays the boot entry
  -> next run: guard sees the new pin in /etc/default/limine and exits, so nothing retries
```

**Impact:** A machine can end up with the pin in `/etc/default/limine` and a boot entry that still lacks `root=`, with no warning shown. This matters more because `1789325478.sh` puts `linux-omarchy` first in the boot order and requests a reboot. That migration's own comment notes that `limine-mkinitcpio` can return success after skipping a failed kernel build.

**Suggested change:** After the rebuild, verify the cmdline that will actually boot, as `preserve_kernel_cmdline_root` does (it checks `/boot/limine.conf` and each `omarchy_linux*.efi` embedded cmdline). Exit non-zero if `root=` is still missing, so the migration stays pending. The crypt-root and unknown-UUID skips also exit 0. Whether those should keep the migration pending, as the migrations guide describes, is a maintainer decision.

**Guard note:** Line 15 treats a failed `limine-entry-tool` call (for example, a refused `sudo` re-exec, with stderr discarded) the same as "no `root=`". On an already pinned machine, that would append a second pin and rebuild. Capturing the output and exiting non-zero on tool failure avoids guessing.

**Repository test:** `test/shell.d/privileged-heredoc-test.sh` passes on the merge base and fails on this head: `migrations/1789840720.sh:73: unquoted heredoc <<EOF_CONF expands values ... reaches /etc/default/limine ... other expansions: boot_params`. The same annotation that `preserve_kernel_cmdline_root` uses, `# omarchy:heredoc-expands paths=none -- <reason>`, placed directly above the heredoc together with the `sudo tee -a` change, made the test pass in a local probe copy.

**PR description:** Comments on #9826 describe a manual archinstall plus Omarchy 3.x bare install, already repaired by hand. A quattro migration does not run on that machine, so `Related #9826` describes the link more accurately than `Fixes`.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Reviewed head `1e54fe7`. Source review of the migration, the migration runner and update entry points, `preserve_kernel_cmdline_root`, and limine-entry-tool 1.37.1 and 1.39.0 (Java config reader and the mkinitcpio hook scripts), plus omarchy-iso and archinstall ESP mount options. Isolated runs covered `privileged-heredoc-test.sh`, `limine-defaults-test.sh` and `upgrade-to-quattro-test.sh` on the merge base and head, and a synthetic harness that ran an adapted copy of the migration with stubbed tools and redirected paths. The migration, bootloader tools and boots were not run on a real machine. The unprivileged-write failure is established from runner source; the harness only approximates root-owned files.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks of single-source claims, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
